useCases: Deploy mid-run recovery — A research agent fanning out to dozens of web fetches is killed by a rolling deploy, and the restarted worker resumes from the last checkpoint instead of refetching.
Lost in-memory handle — A graph keeps an open DB cursor in a Python variable, so after restart only checkpointed state returns and the node must rebuild the cursor from a saved offset.

industries.problem: Multi-hour LLM enrichment pipelines crash partway, and persisted progress avoids reprocessing finished batches and paying for them twice.
Claims agents wait days for documents from customers, and checkpointed state lets the run survive restarts and pick up at the pending step.

useCases: Rate-limited LLM node — A summarization node declares a retry policy for HTTP 429 and timeout errors, with capped attempts and backoff, so the node body holds only the model call.
Payment tool node guarded — A node that charges a card through an API retries only on network timeouts, using an idempotency key so a repeated attempt cannot double-charge.

industries.problem: Order graphs call inventory and shipping APIs that fail briefly; retrying only transient errors avoids lost orders without resubmitting invalid carts.
Agents fetching patient records hit flaky upstream systems; retrying timeouts but never 403 denials keeps access rules intact and runs reliable.

useCases: Fix a refund amount — an agent proposes issue_refund with a wrong order total, the support lead edits it to the right figure, and the edited args pass the same Pydantic schema before the payment call runs.
Correct a drafted email recipient — a reviewer swaps a mistyped address in the send_email args, and the graph re-checks format and an allowed-domain rule before resuming.

industries.problem: An agent picks the right refund action but the wrong amount, and an agent-side edit must still obey refund limits before payment.
An agent proposes a correct restart command against the wrong host, and an engineer's edited target must be checked against the inventory allowlist.

useCases: Crash recovery on a long ingest — a document-processing graph with PostgresSaver resumes from the last saved step after a worker restart, using the same thread_id instead of re-running OCR.
Per-user chat memory — a support bot with SqliteSaver keeps each customer's conversation under its own thread_id, so a returning session reloads prior messages and state.

industries.problem: Multi-day shipment exception workflows must survive deploys and restarts without losing which carrier steps already completed.
Shopper assistants need conversation state kept per customer across sessions so carts and preferences are not lost between visits.

useCases: Per-node timing before fan-out — A research graph's trace shows a single slow retrieval node dominates each run, so the team fixes that node before adding parallel branches.
Checkpoint overhead audit — An agent writing full state to Postgres after every step spends more time saving than computing, so the team checkpoints less often or trims state size.

industries.problem: A product-enrichment graph fanned out to many LLM calls and ran slower, since merge and checkpoint costs outweighed the parallel savings.
A KYC review graph missed its latency target until node timings showed one sanctions-lookup step, not the parallel checks, was the critical path.

useCases: Live trip-planner panel — a React itinerary view re-renders from the full state after each node, so flights, hotels and budget always match the latest graph values.
Hiding internal scratch fields — a graph's output schema leaves out raw tool results and a private reasoning field, so the browser only receives the draft answer and status.

industries.problem: Itinerary pages must show the current plan after every agent step without the client merging partial updates by hand.
Advisor-facing agent state holds account numbers and risk notes that must be filtered out before snapshots reach the customer app.

useCases: PII scrub before tools run — a post_model_hook inspects the model's reply and, if a tool call's arguments contain a raw card number, replaces the call with a refusal message before the tool node executes.
Block disallowed tool calls — a hook on a DevOps agent checks the AI message for a delete_database call and swaps in a message asking for confirmation, so the graph never routes to the tool node.

industries.problem: A model reply may propose a transfer tool call above policy limits, and a hook must stop it before any payment API is reached.
A clinical assistant's reply can include a dosage-changing tool call, and a hook checks it against safe ranges before the call proceeds.

useCases: Parallel evidence gathering — A due-diligence graph sends one company name to separate nodes for news search, filings lookup and sanctions check, then a summary node runs once all three return.
Stalled branch blocks the join — A fan-out calls three vendor price APIs and one hangs with no timeout, so the compare node never runs until the branch gets a timeout and a fallback result.

industries.problem: Flight, hotel and car-rental searches are independent, so running them concurrently and merging once cuts a trip-quote wait to the slowest provider.
Screening a trial candidate needs separate lab, medication and history checks, and eligibility can be decided only after every check has reported.

useCases: Expiring refund approval — a refund over a set amount waits for a manager, and after 24 hours with no reply the run resumes on a deny branch and notifies the customer.
Stale approval on edited action — an approver okays a drafted email to a vendor, the draft is then revised, and the saved approval is rejected because its hash no longer matches.

industries.problem: Production change requests wait on an on-call approver who never answers, so the paused run must expire to a safe no-change default.
A purchase order approved last week is edited to a new supplier or amount, and the old sign-off must not authorize the changed order.

useCases: Cross-thread preference recall — A shopping assistant writes a user's shoe size and preferred brands to a store namespace, so a brand-new thread next week can read them without the old chat history.

Thread-scoped follow-ups — A travel-booking agent uses a checkpointer so "make it the earlier flight" resolves against that thread's messages, while a store keeps the traveler's seat preference across trips.

industries.problem: Returning shoppers must re-explain sizes and style tastes in every new chat, so a store keeps those facts across threads.
A tutoring agent forgets which topics a student struggled with, so a cross-thread store carries learning notes between sessions.

useCases: Pinpoint a slow node — A traced support graph shows the retrieval node takes 9 seconds while the LLM node takes 2, so the team tunes the vector query first.
Debug a wrong tool call — An engineer opens a failed run's trace, sees the router node passed a malformed order ID into the lookup tool, and fixes the prompt.

industries.problem: Compliance reviewers need per-node inputs and outputs to explain why a loan-screening graph made a call, with account data redacted first.
Intermittent failures in a 30-node onboarding agent are hard to find without per-node timing and state changes across runs.

useCases: Abort on tab close — a chat UI's client disconnects mid-stream, so the server cancels the running graph and its pending LLM and tool calls stop billing tokens.
Compensate a half-done booking — a travel agent cancelled after reserving a flight but before the hotel runs cleanup to release the hold and mark the checkpoint as abandoned.

industries.problem: A rider cancels a request while an agent is dispatching, so the driver hold and pending fare authorization must be released.
A provisioning agent is stopped halfway, leaving orphaned VMs and volumes that need teardown so they stop costing money.

useCases: Replay a bad answer — an engineer lists a thread's checkpoints, finds the step where retrieval returned wrong documents, and inspects the state there to see why the final reply went off.
Retention job for chat threads — a support bot's thread accumulates a checkpoint per step across weeks, so a scheduled job deletes older checkpoints to keep load latency and Postgres size down.

industries.problem: Long-running customer threads pile up checkpoints, slowing state loads, so old ones are pruned while recent history stays debuggable.
Reviewers must show how an agent reached a flagged decision, so past states are inspected, with retention limits applied to cap storage.

useCases: Rewrite after a weak first retrieval — a grader node finds the top chunks off-topic for an HR policy question, so a rewrite node adds the policy's formal name and the graph retrieves again.
Capped retrieval loop for a docs assistant — after three retrieve-assess cycles without relevant passages, the graph routes to an answer node that says the docs do not cover it.

industries.problem: Staff ask vague questions about internal runbooks, and one search misses, so rewriting the query and retrying finds the right page before answering.
Literature questions use varying compound names, so a failed first search must be reformulated with synonyms, within a bounded number of retrievals.

useCases: Iterating on a late prompt — a RAG graph's embedding and retrieval nodes reuse cached results while the developer edits only the final answer node's prompt and re-runs.
Key missing a config field — a summarize node is cached on document text alone, so changing the model name or system prompt still returns the stale old summary.

industries.problem: Re-running a contract-analysis graph to tweak one clause-check prompt repeats costly OCR and parsing, which cached upstream nodes avoid.
Rerunning a scraping-and-classify graph while tuning the report step refetches unchanged pages, so caching saves LLM spend and wait time.

useCases: Live progress feed — a document-analysis graph streams one update per node, so the UI shows "OCR done" then "clauses extracted" without resending the whole state.
Delta-driven audit log — a consumer appends each node's emitted changes to an event table in arrival order, then rebuilds the final state by replaying them.

industries.problem: Underwriters wait on long loan-review graphs, and per-node update events show which check just finished without reloading full applicant state.
A video-captioning pipeline has many stages, and streaming only each stage's changes lets editors see progress cheaply and in the right order.

useCases: Edit a message in place — a chat UI lets a user revise an earlier question, and the new HumanMessage reuses the same id so add_messages replaces that entry rather than duplicating it.

Tool-calling chat history — an agent node returns an AIMessage with tool calls and a ToolNode returns ToolMessages, and add_messages appends both so the next model call sees the full ordered exchange.

industries.problem: Agent corrections to a sent reply must overwrite the earlier message by id, or the transcript shows contradictory duplicates.
A tutoring bot must keep every student and tutor turn in order across nodes, and revised answers must replace prior ones without repeats.

useCases: Reusable refund-check subgraph — a returns graph and a support graph both call one tested eligibility workflow, mapping order_id and policy_region in and a verdict field back out.
Isolated research step with private state — a report graph embeds a search-and-rank subgraph whose scratch queries and raw hits stay inside, returning only a ranked source list.

industries.problem: Loan, card and account flows all need the same identity-verification steps, and one nested workflow avoids copying and drifting logic.
An editorial pipeline has a fact-check stage owned by another team, so it is built and tested alone and plugged in with mapped fields.

useCases: Append messages from parallel tools — two tool nodes in one step each return a ToolMessage, and an add_messages reducer keeps both in the history instead of the last one.
Merge findings from fan-out workers — three research branches write source URLs to one list channel, and an operator.add reducer concatenates them so the writer node sees every source.

industries.problem: Parallel scraping branches each return competitor findings, and without a reducer only the last branch's list would survive to the report.
Sentiment and intent nodes both add notes to a ticket in one step, and a merge reducer keeps both instead of dropping one.

useCases: Typed state for a support triage graph — a StateGraph declares a TypedDict with messages, ticket_category and priority, so classify, retrieve and draft nodes all read and write the same fields.
Silent drop from a typo'd key — a draft node returns {"reply_text": ...} while the schema field is "draft", so the update is dropped and the review node sees an empty draft.

industries.problem: Claims intake graphs pass policy data, photos and fraud flags between steps, and a fixed state schema keeps every node using the same field names.
Resume screening agents pass candidate data between parse, score and outreach nodes, so a compiled graph with a declared schema keeps the pipeline consistent.

useCases: Summarize each uploaded file — a node reads a list of PDFs in state and uses Send to start one summarize_doc instance per file, then a reducer merges the summaries into one list.

Per-chunk claim extraction — a long contract is split into a runtime-determined number of sections, each sent to an extract_clauses node, and results are appended via an operator.add reducer before ranking.

industries.problem: Discovery batches contain an unknown number of documents, so each needs its own review branch and the findings must merge without overwriting.
A survey export holds a varying number of free-text responses, and per-response tagging must run in parallel then combine into one theme tally.

useCases: Trim by token budget — a support agent's thread passes 40 turns, so a trim step keeps the system prompt and latest messages that fit the window before each model call.
Summarize old turns, keep open calls — a coding agent condenses early chat into a summary message while keeping an AIMessage tool call and its pending ToolMessage together.

industries.problem: Month-long ticket threads outgrow the model window, so old turns need summarizing without dropping the open refund promise.
Coding agents run long tool loops, and cutting history mid-call leaves a tool result with no matching call, which the API rejects.

useCases: Disambiguate a record — a CRM node finds two matching customers, interrupts with both, and continues with the one chosen.
Repeated side effect — a node posts a Slack alert before interrupt(), so resume re-runs it and posts twice.

industries.problem: An underwriting node hits a missing employer field and must request it from a loan officer without restarting the case.
A dispatch node finds two eligible technicians and needs a coordinator to pick one before assigning the job.

useCases: Dedup-merge reducer for parallel tags — two classifier nodes in one step both propose labels for a support ticket, and a set-union reducer keeps each label once instead of duplicates.
Keyed score merge for parallel graders — three evaluator nodes write rubric scores to one dict field, and a custom reducer merges by key so no grader's entry overwrites another's.

industries.problem: Parallel fraud, coverage and damage-estimate nodes all write flags to one claim field, and without a reducer only one node's flags would survive.
Résumé-parsing, skills-match and reference-check nodes run together and write to one candidate record, so a reducer must combine their notes without loss.

useCases: Restart-survival test — a deploy kills the worker mid-run, and a test confirms the new process resumes the same thread from PostgresSaver at the last completed step.
Swap InMemorySaver before launch — a prototype's graph loses every open thread on each redeploy, so the team moves to a Postgres checkpointer and sizes its connection pool.

industries.problem: Multi-day claim workflows must keep their saved state across deploys and crashes instead of restarting from step one.
A dispatch agent writing a checkpoint every step needs a low-latency backend, since slow storage delays each routing decision.

useCases: Route a triage verdict — a classify node writes category=billing|technical|abuse to state, and a routing function maps each value to its own node with a fallback for unknown labels.
Unit-test the router without a model — a pytest feeds hand-built state dicts like {"score": 0.4} into the routing function and asserts it returns "escalate", so no LLM call is needed.

industries.problem: A symptom-intake graph must send red-flag answers to a nurse node and routine ones to scheduling, with no unhandled outcome.
Claim state with amount and fraud score must route to auto-approve, adjuster review or SIU, and a mistyped branch name would fail mid-run.

useCases: Update only the changed key — an extract_invoice node returns {"vendor": "Acme", "total": 480} and leaves messages and attachments untouched, so later nodes see everything else as it was.
Parallel siblings stay intact — a sentiment node and a language-detect node run in one step, each returning only its own field, so neither clobbers the other's write.

industries.problem: Parallel nodes fill allergies and medication fields on one patient record, and returning the full record would erase a sibling's entry.
Address-validation and carrier-rate nodes run together on a shipment, so each must return just its own fields to avoid overwriting the other.

useCases: Kill the worker mid-payment — a test crashes the process after a charge node commits but before the checkpoint advances, resumes the thread, and asserts the gateway saw one charge.
Replay a duplicate webhook — a test delivers the same shipment-confirmed event twice to a resumed order graph and asserts one email and one inventory decrement.

industries.problem: A crash between charging a card and saving the checkpoint can re-run the charge on resume, so tests must prove idempotency keys prevent double billing.
Carrier webhooks arrive twice or after a worker restart, and a resumed tracking graph must not create duplicate pickups or notifications.

useCases: Per-request DB client and user ID — a support graph receives a Postgres connection pool and the caller's user_id as run context, so nodes query with it and neither lands in any checkpoint.
Resume under the right caller — a paused approval run is resumed with the resuming session's tenant_id passed fresh as context, rather than reading a stale tenant_id saved in state.

industries.problem: One agent serves many tenants, so each run must receive its tenant ID and API clients without storing them in replayable state.
A clinician-facing agent must act under the current clinician's identity on resume, not one frozen in an older checkpoint.
A claims agent pauses for adjuster review and must not resubmit the payout request when the node re-runs on resume.
Scores from parallel interviewer-summary nodes must combine into one list, not let the last branch overwrite the rest.

useCases: Redact PII before persisting — a checkpoint hook masks card numbers and SSNs in a support graph's state, so no raw values land in the Postgres checkpoint table.
Compress state on write — a serialization hook gzips a large scraped-HTML field before each checkpoint is saved, and the read path decompresses it before nodes run.

industries.problem: Patient notes in graph state must not be stored in plain text, so a write hook masks identifiers before any checkpoint hits disk.
Account numbers in a loan graph's state would be copied into every checkpoint, so redacting once at write time keeps stored history compliant.

useCases: Try a different prompt from a past step — a developer picks the checkpoint before a planner node, edits the state's instructions, and resumes as a fork to compare plans against the original run.
Fork warns about repeated email — an agent already sent a confirmation email before the fork point, so resuming the new thread from there sends a second one unless that node is guarded.

industries.problem: A trip-planning agent picked a poor itinerary, so planners fork from the pre-search step with new constraints and compare options without losing the first plan.
Analysts want to rerun an agent's trade-rationale pipeline from a mid-run checkpoint with altered inputs while keeping the original run intact as a reference.

useCases: Fix a wrong extracted field — a reviewer finds an invoice agent saved the wrong vendor_id at a checkpoint, patches that one value, and resumes so later nodes use the corrected record.
Schema-breaking patch caught on resume — an operator writes a string into an integer retry_count field at a checkpoint, and the thread only fails when it resumes, so the edit is reverted.

industries.problem: An agent misreads an invoice total mid-run, and a clerk must correct that value and resume rather than reprocess the entire batch.
A trial-data agent stores a wrongly coded adverse-event field, so a coordinator corrects it at the checkpoint and the audit trail shows who changed what.

useCases: Research-and-critique loop — a writer node drafts an answer, a critic node scores it, and a conditional edge returns to the writer until the score passes or a retry cap is hit.
Inspect a stalled run — an engineer reads the compiled graph's nodes and edges plus the latest checkpoint to see which node an agent stopped at and why.

industries.problem: Code-fix agents must loop between patching and running tests until green, which a linear chain cannot express without hand-rolled retry code.
Long-running ticket workflows need an inspectable path and a resumable position, so a stuck case can be traced to a node and continued.

useCases: Reject a bad type — a grader returns confidence as "high" for a float field, and the Pydantic state model fails before routing.
Port graph to TypeScript — a Python TypedDict is redeclared via Annotation.Root so the Node service keeps the same fields.

industries.problem: Triage nodes exchange vitals and medication doses, and typed fields stop a dose string being read as a number.
A Python agent backend and a TypeScript storefront API must agree on cart and order fields in a shopping assistant.

useCases: Charge after approval \u2014 a refund node moves the payment call below interrupt() so the manager's resume triggers exactly one gateway request, not one per replay.
Idempotency key from thread \u2014 a node that sends a welcome SMS derives its key from thread_id plus step name, so a retried node reuses it and the provider drops the duplicate.

industries.problem: A retried order node can create a second shipment label or charge, so writes must be guarded to avoid duplicate fulfillment.
An onboarding graph that pauses for manager sign-off can re-create accounts or resend offer letters unless each write is repeat-safe.

useCases: Validate-then-route in one return — a validate_address node returns Command(update={"address_ok": False, "errors": errs}, goto="ask_user") so the failure note and next step are set together.
Retry counter with escalation — a tool-calling node returns Command(update={"attempts": n+1}, goto="escalate") once n hits 3, otherwise goto="call_tool", with no separate conditional edge.

industries.problem: A fraud-check node must record its risk score and send high-risk orders to manual review in one step, without a separate router.
A triage node must save the detected issue type and pick the matching resolver node, keeping the label and the handoff consistent.

useCases: Show nested agent progress in a UI — a chat front end streams with subgraphs enabled so a research subgraph's tool calls appear under its own label instead of a long pause.
Attribute tokens to the right sub-workflow — a log consumer reads the namespace on each streamed chunk to separate a planner subgraph's output from a nested coder subgraph's.

industries.problem: A coding assistant's nested test-and-fix subgraph runs for minutes, and users need to see which inner step is running instead of a frozen stream.
A support dashboard must show which nested escalation workflow produced each event so supervisors can audit its steps live and afterward.

useCases: Inject account context — a pre_model_hook on a billing agent reads the customer's plan and open invoices from state and prepends them as a system message just before each model turn.
Reorder retrieved passages — before every model call in a RAG agent, the hook sorts fetched document chunks by relevance score so the strongest evidence sits last, nearest the question.

industries.problem: A support agent's loop re-reads bulky diagnostic logs each turn, so a per-call hook must shrink them before the model sees them.
Case-law agents gather many cited passages, and a hook must reorder and cap them each turn so key rulings fit the context window.

useCases: Approve before the refund node — a support graph compiled with interrupt_before=["issue_refund"] stops there so an agent can read the drafted amount and resume or reject.
Review a draft after generation — a compliance-email graph uses interrupt_after=["draft_email"] so a reviewer reads the finished text in state before the send node runs.

industries.problem: A wire-transfer agent must stop before the release node so an officer can check payee and amount without editing node code.
Generated promotional copy must pause after the drafting node so a medical-legal reviewer can read it before any publishing step.

useCases: Prompt rewrite A/B — Run the old and new summarization prompts over the same 200 support tickets and have an LLM judge pick the better summary, with output order randomized.
Model swap check — Compare a cheaper model against the current one on a dataset of SQL-generation questions, with reviewers choosing the preferred query without seeing which model wrote it.

industries.problem: Lawyers must decide if a revised contract-summary prompt reads better than the old one, though no single summary has a clear correct answer.
Teams tuning product-description generators need to rank two versions on identical items when no reference text exists to score against.

useCases: Zero-code tracing rollout — Set the tracing environment variables on an existing LangChain service in staging and immediately see every chain, retriever and LLM call as nested runs, with no code changes.
Redacting sensitive inputs — After auto-tracing captures full prompts containing customer emails, the team inspects the run tree and adds input masking or turns tracing off for that chain.

industries.problem: Auto-tracing every chain call can store patient symptoms in traces, so teams must audit run inputs and mask them before enabling it.
A shopping assistant built on LangChain gets instant visibility into slow retriever and tool calls without engineers instrumenting each step.

useCases: Sequential report pipeline with @task — a nightly script fetches data, drafts a summary and emails it as plain Python steps, and each @task result is saved so a crash skips finished calls on rerun.

Choose functional over StateGraph — a team weighing a three-step ingest flow writes it as an @entrypoint with ordinary if and for statements, accepting that no node-and-edge diagram can be drawn from it.

industries.problem: A linear ETL job with a few LLM enrichment calls needs to resume after failure without re-calling completed steps or maintaining a full graph definition.
A draft, fact-check and format workflow is mostly linear, so plain decorated functions give durability with less boilerplate than declaring nodes and edges.

useCases: Negative-feedback review queue — A rule matches production runs where users clicked thumbs-down and adds them to an annotation queue so a reviewer sees them without searching.
Sampled online scoring — A rule samples 5% of successful chatbot runs and applies an LLM-as-judge groundedness evaluator, keeping cost low while a quality trend builds.

industries.problem: Low-rated or escalated bot conversations reach human reviewers automatically instead of being buried among thousands of routine chats.
Runs where a clinical summarizer output fails a safety evaluator are routed to a clinician review queue without staff scanning every trace.

useCases: Pairwise prompt comparison — Reviewers see two candidate answers to the same support question side by side and pick the better one against a written rubric.
Low-score triage queue — Production runs with thumbs-down or low automated scores are routed to a queue where domain experts label failure type and write corrected outputs.

industries.problem: Clinicians review LLM-drafted patient message replies against a safety rubric before the replies are trusted at scale.
Attorneys score contract-clause summaries for accuracy using shared criteria, so quality is judged consistently across reviewers.

useCases: Tone rubric for support replies — A judge prompt scores each drafted reply 1-5 for empathy and policy-appropriate phrasing, run over a 200-example dataset before each prompt revision.
Judge calibration against human labels — Reviewers label 50 summaries as faithful or not, then the team compares the judge's verdicts to theirs and rewrites the rubric until disagreements shrink.

industries.problem: Contract-summary quality such as completeness and faithfulness can't be regex-checked, so a rubric judge flags dropped clauses for lawyer review.
Tutoring bot explanations must be age-appropriate and pedagogically sound, which a judge scores at scale while teachers spot-check its verdicts.

useCases: First trace smoke test — A developer wires tracing into a new tool-calling agent, runs one prompt on a laptop, and checks the trace shows each tool call before adding more steps.
Dev project isolation — An engineer sets a dedicated dev project name in the local environment so debugging runs never mix with the production project's latency and error charts.

industries.problem: Developers prototyping a note summarizer must not send real patient text to a trace store, so they test with synthetic notes in a dev project.
Experimental local runs of a loan-FAQ bot would skew production error and latency dashboards unless they land in a separate project.

useCases: Sampled groundedness scoring — Run a reference-free hallucination check on 5% of production answers from a support RAG bot, capped per day to bound judge cost.
Thread-level frustration flag — Score whole chat threads once they go idle for a user-frustration evaluator, and alert when the failure rate climbs after a prompt release.

industries.problem: Compliance needs ongoing checks that live chatbot replies avoid giving financial advice, without paying to judge every conversation.
A tutoring assistant drifts on real student questions, and no reference answers exist to score them, so quality needs sampled live checks.

useCases: Rollback after a tone regression — Support complaints rise after a system prompt edit, so the team compares commit history, finds the change, and restores the previous commit in the hub.
Pinning production to a commit — The deployed agent pulls its prompt by a specific commit hash instead of latest, so edits in the playground can't silently change live answers.

industries.problem: Auditors ask which exact loan-explanation prompt produced a customer reply, and commit history ties each output to a reviewed wording.
Several people edit one shared triage prompt, and without commits a sudden drop in routing accuracy can't be traced to a change.

useCases: Hotfix a tone problem live — A support bot starts sounding curt after a model update, so a prompt engineer edits the system prompt in the hub and the service pulls the new version without a deploy.
Roll back a bad prompt version — After a prompt edit raises refusal rates, the team repoints the production tag to the previous commit instead of reverting and redeploying application code.

industries.problem: Compliance wording in assistant prompts changes often, and a central versioned history shows who edited a live prompt and when, even without a code review.
Product managers must update seasonal policy text in itinerary-bot prompts quickly without waiting on an engineering release cycle.

useCases: Latency regression hunt — Filter traces by tag and latency over 10 seconds, then compare a slow run with a fast run of the same query to spot the extra tool call.
Pre/post deploy diff — Pick the same user question traced before and after a model version bump and view both runs side by side to see which retrieval step changed.

industries.problem: Compliance asks why a loan-FAQ bot gave different answers last week, so engineers filter by metadata and diff the two runs.
An itinerary agent began calling the pricing tool twice after a prompt edit, and comparing traces shows exactly where the extra call began.

useCases: Tracing a custom reranker — Decorate the in-house function that reorders retrieved chunks so its inputs, scores and latency appear as a child run under the RAG request.
Timing a parsing step — Decorate the function that turns raw PDF text into structured fields so slow or failing extraction shows up as its own run inside the agent trace.

industries.problem: Claim-triage agents call in-house policy lookup code that framework tracing misses, so decorating it reveals which step slowed or altered a decision.
A route-planning assistant calls custom rate-calculation functions, and decorating them shows the inputs behind a bad shipping quote inside the trace.

useCases: Residency-driven hosting choice — An EU bank's agent traces contain account details that must stay in-region, so the platform team picks self-hosted LangSmith inside its own VPC over the SaaS cloud.

Hybrid split for a small team — A startup keeps the LangSmith control plane hosted for fast setup while agent runtime and trace payloads stay in its own cloud account, avoiding a full self-hosted cluster.

industries.problem: Traces with account data cannot leave approved regions, so deployment must keep trace storage inside the bank's own infrastructure.
Agencies on air-gapped or restricted networks cannot send prompts to a vendor cloud and must run and patch the platform themselves.

useCases: Splitting a refund agent across three tools — A team builds retrieval and tool calls with LangChain, runs the approval loop as a LangGraph graph, and uses LangSmith only to trace and score the runs.
Tracing a hand-rolled agent — An engineer whose service calls a model SDK directly and has no LangChain code still adds LangSmith tracing to inspect latency and token use per step.

industries.problem: Claims-triage teams need to tell whether a bad routing decision came from a component, graph logic or evaluation setup before fixing it.
A dispatch assistant with multi-step rerouting needs clear ownership of building, running and inspecting so on-call engineers debug the right layer.

useCases: Thumbs-down tied to a run ID — A chat UI sends the run ID with each thumbs-up or down click, so a rating lands on the exact trace that produced that answer.
Satisfaction vs correctness keys — A docs assistant logs a 'helpful' score from users and a separate 'factually_correct' score from a reviewer who checks the cited page.

industries.problem: Travelers rate a trip-planning bot's reply well even when the quoted baggage rule is wrong, so satisfaction can't stand in for accuracy.
Employees correct a policy bot's answer about leave, and attaching that fix to the producing run lets engineers see the retrieved policy version.

useCases: Retire outdated examples — After a refund policy change, an engineer finds dataset examples whose reference answers cite the old 30-day window and corrects or removes them.
Version before editing — Before rewriting 40 expected outputs, the team tags the current dataset version so earlier experiment scores are not compared with the new set.
